doc.title: Buddy Burns and Frank Pasley Interview, 1968-09-23

title: Alex, the one-legged piano player
summary: They try to recall the real name of an older one-legged district pianist.

story.theme_name: Pianists: who played, who influenced whom
story.community_name: Who played piano: the pianists musicians remembered

blocks.x: Well, they was all way older. Alex, see, oh, yeah.
Alex? No. I did not give it to him. No, I did not give it to him. Oh, yeah. Do you know his complete name?
His name was, uh, uh, uh.
No, not Lionel. Not Lee Maugh. He was named, oh, sure. He had a funny kind of name. But nobody used it, you know.

Alexei, yeah. He had a style of his own, too. He played in the district, you know, all kind of old blues and stuff. Oh, yeah. Yeah. He was a pretty old man. He was way older than me. Jesus. That little boy, he was a man playing. He must have been 30 years old then. When I was 10 or 12, something like that. Yeah. He had to be about 30. He was pretty old. Yeah. One leg.
Yeah, yeah. One leg. One leg. Yeah. You can't recall his first name.

Yeah, but I was trying to get his first name. Nobody hardly ever used it, but I didn't know it. His first name. It was a real old time. Did you? Some little Robertson. Did you get him? Robertson? Robertson piano. What's his first name? Samla. Samla? No. Samla. That's another old timer. What?
